title: Two-monotone endpoint rays and the higher-order parity obstruction

publication.repair_reason: Strengthen the all-orders obstruction interface so it explicitly asserts a negative finite prime-set difference rather than only existence of a prime set.

mathematical_claims: For each prime p, the literal response difference r_n-r_(pn) is pointwise nonnegative.
For distinct primes p,r, the literal mixed response difference r_n-r_(pn)-r_(rn)+r_(prn) is pointwise nonnegative.
Exact finite placement reindexing gives nonnegative first and second multiplicative prime differences of the endpoint ray weights.
The exact N=12 third prime difference is negative, and adjoining primes above the horizon extends the failure to every order k>=3.
First/second monotonicity plus factor-one-half insertion contraction do not logically imply a nonpositive complete parity sum, as shown by the six-label rank fixture.
